title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on oMLX: 8 concurrent 252K slots on a 128 GB Mac
slug_note: The Mac answer to the 180B MoE: oMLX pages the PLE table through an SSD tier and holds eight ~252K orchestrator slots, 60.9 tok/s solo decode with MTP on.

variation.quant_detail: NVFP4 weights converted to oMLX 'flash oQ4e' with SSD-paged PLE tables

engine.config: oMLX 0.6.4 single process: SSD tier for PLE tables, self-managed prefix promotion, MTP spec-dec on

requirements.notes: 69 GB booted idle; 102 GB peak during dual-252K cold fill; ~9.25 GB KV per 252K slot.

steps.text: Follow the oMLX recipe in the repo
Keep the PLE tables on fast SSD; they page in and out
Enable MTP speculative decode for the quoted solo decode

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: W1 dual ~252K concurrent cold prefill wall (488.4 s for the second, spread 4.73 s = true concurrency), measured prompt_tokens 240,393 each, 2026-08-31

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: peak phys_footprint during dual-252K cold fill (G1 run) = the planning number against the 107.5 GB Metal cap; W1 peaked at 98 GB

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: booted idle footprint with the flash oQ4e weights paged in; ~73 GB steady with all 8 HTTP slots resident after orchestrator KV auto-tiers to SSD

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: re-promoting a 252K prefix from the SSD tier (a self-managed 185.8 GB LRU) vs ~229 s for a full re-prefill on an LRU miss

measurements.note: solo decode with MTP speculative decode ON for this checkpoint on this box, vs ~86 tok/s with it off - the measured reason mtp_enabled=false

measurements.note: 27B dense 4x118K per-stream wall spread with chunked prefill OFF (304/1225/1240/1243 s FIFO staircase); with chunked ON the spread is 25.6 s and every stream TTFT ~4 s

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: worst TTFT across six worker prefills over hot orchestrators (range 0.05-0.66 s, measured prompt_tokens 30,585 TDD and 61,089 coder/auditor)

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: KV slot rate per ~252K orchestrator slot (~1.2 GB per 32K slot, ~2.3 GB per 64K slot); static worst case with nothing tiered ~97-99 GB

measurements.method: oMLX recipe runs: dual-252K cold prefill walls, solo decode with MTP, prefix re-promotion
measurements.note: longest observed memory-planner tick during the W1 dual fill (the pair was 11.26 s and 1.12 s; range across the box ~1-25 s)

caveats: This is oMLX, not stock mlx-lm: the runtime carries the qwen4_exp/PLE paging that stock MLX lacks, so the recipe is runtime-specific.
Cold-fill walls (483.6 s for dual ~252K) are the price of the SSD tier; warm re-promotion at 8.7 s is the number that makes the lane usable.
The builder repo tags its own license as 'other'; the weights lineage is Qwen Apache-2.0.
Builder runtimes carry their own terms on top of the weights (Mia's scripts are AGPL-3.0).
